Page 1 
 
 
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE   
   
This is the portion of the meeting set aside for general public comment directly related to City business, for matters that do 
not appear on this evening’s agenda. If you are here for a specific agenda item that is under Unfinished Business or New 
Business, please wait until we reach that item. Items under First Reading & Referral will be discussed when they return 
under Unfinished Business, and we will hear public comment at that time.  Public comment requires a person to state your 
name and whether you are a resident of Bangor. The City Council has adopted a Public Comment Policy that we will 
adhere to. Statements during public comment should respect the dignity and seriousness of the proceeding, and individuals 
will be restricted to speaking once. Obscene, truly threatening, or overly repetitive comments will be deemed out of order 
and will be interrupted and removed. Topics that are considered out of order also include matters that are in litigation, 
individual employees or employee groups discussing matters for which complaint or grievance procedures are in place, 
personal disputes between the speaker and another resident not germane to City business, support for or opposition to any 
candidate for political office, and personnel complaints pertaining to individual City employees. There is a time limit of 
three minutes per speaker, and the total time allowed for general public comment regarding City business will be limited to 
no more than one hour. The public comment period is for City Council members to listen and not to respond or debate 
with persons. If you do not live in Bangor or own property in Bangor, please allow those who do to have the opportunity to 
speak first. If you’d like to offer comment on any item directly related to City business not appearing on the regular 
agenda, you may approach the podium. Alternatively, Councilors may be reached via email 
at councilors@bangormaine.gov. (A link to the adopted public comment policy can be found on the City’s website.)

BECK 
    
Executive Summary: This Resolve will authorize the City Manager to accept and appropriate a total of 
$3,048,959 in grant funds for the Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) Program for a coverage period of 
October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2027.  
 
Public Health and Community Services, WIC Nutrition Program currently services a monthly average of 
2,700 participants and has been operating the program since 1974.  The proposed agreement provides 
$841,177 in administrative funding for WIC, Breastfeeding Peer Counseling (BFPC), and Farmers Market 
Nutrition Program (FMNP) services and $2,207,782 for food dollar costs, for a total of $3,048,959.

BECK 
    
Executive Summary: This Resolve will authorize the appropriation of Customer Facility Charge (CFC) 
funds for planning efforts associated with the consolidated rental car facility (CONRAC) in the amount of 
$222,040. 
 
The Airport implemented a CFC program earlier this year to plan, design, build, and operate a consolidated 
facility for rental car operations. The project aims at increasing capacity, upgrading facilities, and 
improving passenger experience. 
 
The work will be performed by airport consultants, Mead & Hunt, under its 5-year comprehensive airport 
engineering services contract. This project is included in the Airport’s Master Plan and 5-year Capital 
Improvement Plan. 
 
This item was reviewed and recommended for approval at the Business & Economic Development 
Committee on October 19, 2026.

Executive Summary: This Resolve would appropriate up to $65,000 from the undesignated fund balance 
for the purpose of funding a Director of Transit.  
 
The Community Connector has been a long-time division under the City Manager's Office, with the City 
Manager serving at the executive-level department head overseeing Community Connector operations. 
Given the growth of the Community Connector, including increased federal regulatory requirements and 
large projects, it is necessary for there to be a stand-alone Department Head-level position that leads the 
Community Connector. By creating a new Director of Transit position, the City acknowledges the critical 
importance of its public transportation system to the City and its residents.

Summary 
This ordinance would amend the Land Development Code, District Map to re-zone the property at Map-Lot 
R28-003-A, located at 56 Godsoe Road, from Industry and Service District (I&S) to Urban Industry District 
(UID). The total area requested to be changed is approximately 4.73 acres. The applicant and owner of record 
is Fedex Freight, Inc. 
This area is within the growth boundary shown in the 2022 Comprehensive Plan and the future land use map 
in the Plan shows this property in the Industrial area which consists of “a range of industrial and commercial 
uses that benefit from proximity to I-95 and the associated highway interchange”.

CITY COUNCIL ORDINANCE 
Date: November 9, 2026 
Assigned to Councilor:  
ORDINANCE, Amending Chapter 165, Land Development Code, District Map to Re-Zone a Property Located at 
56 Godsoe Road from Industry and Service District (I&S) to Urban Industry District (UID). 
WHEREAS, the land uses around the property consists primarily of a mix of industrial and residential; 
WHEREAS, the zoning around the property consists primarily of Industry & Service District (I&S), Urban 
Industry District (UID), and Urban Residence District 1 (URD-1); 
WHEREAS, the 2022 Comprehensive Plan and the future land use map in the Plan shows this property in the 
Industrial area which consists of “a range of industrial and commercial uses that benefit from proximity to I-95 
and the associated highway interchange”;  
BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF BANGOR AS FOLLOWS, THAT 
Chapter 165 of the Code of the City of Bangor, District Map, is amended to reclassify a portion of the property 
at Map-Lot R28-003-A, located at 56 Godsoe Road, from Industry and Service District (I&S) to Urban Industry 
District (UID). The total area requested to be changed is approximately 4.73 acres and is shown in the 
attached exhibit.

Making an Appropriation from Undesignated Fund Balance in the Amount of Up to $65,000 to Fund a Director 
of Transit
This resolve would appropriate up to $65,000 from the undesignated fund balance for the purpose of 
funding a Director of Transit.  
The Community Connector has been a long-time division under the City Manager's Office, with the 
City Manager serving at the executive-level department head overseeing Community Connector 
operations. Given the growth of the Community Connector, including increased federal regulatory 
requirements and large projects, it is necessary for there to be a stand-alone Department Head-level 
position that leads the Community Connector. By creating a new Director of Transit position, the City 
acknowledges the critical importance of its public transportation system to the City and its residents.
